title: Row order: groups, joins and `unique` keep no order unless asked
verdict: order only with `maintain_order`; a join's default order may change between runs
description: `group_by` keeps the order of the groups consistent with the input only with `maintain_order=True` (which also blocks the streaming engine); rows within a group always keep their order. A join's `maintain_order` defaults to `"none"`: the ordering might differ across Polars versions or between runs, and the docs say not to rely on an observed order.

Float sums depend on the summation tree: pairwise, Kahan when grouped, plain across chunks (polars-sum-float), so chunking and the thread count can change their last bits. The docs do not say so; `sum` only documents that small integers are cast to Int64.
Leads: probes of a float `sum` and `group_by` order at POLARS_MAX_THREADS 1 and N, in memory and streaming; py-polars/tests/unit/operations/test_group_by.py and tests/unit/streaming/.
reference: The reference compares results as bags, so row order outside a sort is free; `sum_order` is open and allowed within the plan's bound (polars-sum-float).
